title: RETURNING Clause
description:
## RETURNING
Normally INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE don't show you what they changed. RETURNING fixes that - it returns the affected rows.
```sql
INSERT INTO servers (name, status)
VALUES ('new-server', 'pending')
RETURNING *;
```
This inserts the row AND shows you what was inserted - including the auto-generated id.

Works with UPDATE and DELETE too:
```sql
UPDATE servers SET status = 'running'
WHERE name = 'new-server'
RETURNING id, name, status;

DELETE FROM servers
WHERE status = 'dead'
RETURNING *;
```

## Assignment:
Insert a new ticket with title 'Server room flooding' and assigned_to 'Steve'. Use RETURNING to show the id, title, and assigned_to of the inserted row.
setupCode: CREATE TABLE tickets (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT, assigned_to TEXT); INSERT INTO tickets VALUES (1, 'Disk full', 'Alice'), (2, 'Memory leak', 'Bob');
starterCode: -- Insert and return the new ticket
expectedOutput:
id | title | assigned_to
3 | Server room flooding | Steve
